lint.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Write-Output 'No dedicated lint command for this Swift package yet.'"

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: On native Windows missions, the startup procedure should allow `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .factory/windows-swift-env.ps1 -CheckOnly` as the first-class environment check when `bash`/WSL is unavailable, instead of assuming `.factory/init.sh` can run everywhere.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Three rerun reviews (`fix-input-routing-observable-assertions-round2`, `fix-resize-dpi-propagation-test-round2`, and `fix-refresh-rate-timer-observability-round2`) independently reported that `.factory/init.sh` is a bash wrapper and failed on this Windows machine until the worker switched to `windows-swift-env.ps1 -CheckOnly`.

rejectedObservations.observation: Add a new library note that workers should use `.factory/windows-swift-env.ps1` for Swift commands on Windows.
Record the bash-wrapper startup gap again as a separate recommendation for `runtime-host-worker`.
rejectedObservations.reason: duplicate; the issue is a general Windows startup-procedure problem, not specific to one worker skill
